summary: Candidate public inputs for New Brunswick hospitals are strongest for quarterly staffing coverage, not task-level minutes. The New Jersey reports cover RWJUH and Saint Peter’s at hospital/unit/quarter level and include ED staffing and patient counts; their own documentation warns that they omit several allied-health roles and do not account for patient need. No verified local task-duration dataset was found. Treat task dependencies and duration distributions as pending institutional collection or clearly labeled external benchmarks, not local measurements.

sources.title: New Jersey Hospital Patient Care Staffing Quarterly Reports
sources.geography: New Jersey general hospitals; query the records for Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital (CCN 310038) and Saint Peter’s University Hospital (CCN 310070). Middlesex County is represented by those hospital records, not county-level task observations.
sources.period: Quarterly reports summarizing monthly reported averages over three-month periods; available report dates require selection/query on the site.
sources.grain: Hospital × inpatient unit type × quarter for patient-to-staff ratios; ED daily staff and patient counts are summarized in the quarterly report; respiratory care practitioner daily counts.
useful_fields: staff category (RN, LPN, UAP, as reported)
observed_facts: NJDOH states that reports provide inpatient unit staffing ratios, ED daily staff and patient counts, and daily respiratory care practitioner counts.
Reports are based on monthly hospital averages derived from daily staffing forms.

The state cautions against comparing hospitals because staffing need, patient services, policies, and physical layout are not accounted for in the ratio data; reports omit roles including social workers and case managers.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the public hospital selector to retrieve RWJUH and Saint Peter’s reports for a bounded period (for example, the latest four available quarters); record the displayed reporting period, unit labels, staffing categories, and ED values, and save the source page/report URL and retrieval date. Do not convert ratios to task minutes or interpret omitted roles as zero.
limitations: No direct downloadable file/API URL was verified; this is a public interactive query.
Staffing counts and ratios do not provide task durations, task mix, patient acuity, interpreter demand, transport workload, or social-work coverage.
Site instructions say daily forms are retained by hospitals for three years and available upon request to the hospitals; this is not evidence that those forms are publicly downloadable.
Public page does not establish redistribution license terms; preserve attribution and have rights reviewed.

sources.title: Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project (HCUP) databases
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
sources.geography: National and participating-state encounter data. New Jersey-specific SID/SEDD availability is not confirmed by the inspected page; not a verified source for the two named hospitals.
sources.period: Annual database releases; the inspected overview states data begin in 1988 but does not identify a current release for New Jersey.
sources.grain: Encounter-level inpatient stay, ED visit, or outpatient service record depending on database product.
observed_facts: AHRQ describes HCUP as a family of encounter data products covering inpatient stays, ED visits, and ambulatory surgery/services.
The AHRQ overview says state and national databases can be purchased through the HCUP Central Distributor.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Check the HCUP participating-state and product pages for New Jersey SID and SEDD availability and the current release years; if available, follow the distributor’s access and training process and verify permitted use before acquisition. Use encounter variables only to stratify simulated need or flow; they do not supply staff task durations.
limitations: No task × skill × patient need × shift records or care-minute fields were established by the inspected overview.
Purchase/access and state participation are not verified for the desired New Jersey products.
Encounter administrative records cannot be treated as direct measures of nursing, interpreter, social-work, or transport labor.

sources.title: Hospital Patient Care Staff Reporting and Posting Instructions Manual
sources.geography: New Jersey licensed hospitals and nursing homes; reporting instructions are statewide rather than Middlesex-specific.
sources.period: Current manual version/date not verified from the inspected page.
sources.grain: Reporting definitions and forms for facility-reported staffing levels, rather than observations of individual tasks.
observed_facts: NJDOH states that licensed hospitals and nursing homes must disclose direct-care staffing and report staffing-level information to the department.
The state page lists a hospital reporting and posting instructions manual.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Open the linked manual and confirm its version, applicable form fields, shift/unit definitions, and calculation method before using it to interpret quarterly reports. Record the manual URL and version alongside any extracted staffing data.
limitations: The instructions page was found in search results but the manual itself was not opened or inspected within this task’s page limit; field details and current version remain unverified.
Definitions and reporting forms do not establish task durations, interpreter services, social work, or transport workload.
Rights and redistribution terms for the manual/data were not independently established.

missing_inputs: Observed ED task inventory with explicit role, prerequisite, and handoff fields across nursing, interpreter, social work, and transport.
Local task duration and variation by shift, acuity/context, language support, and resource availability.
Interpreter encounter counts, mode, language, wait/connection time, and duration for either hospital.
Local social-work and transport staffing/availability and task-level throughput.
Current report-quarter selection and downloadable artifact details for both named hospitals.
Independent review of applicable source rights and hospital-specific applicability.
simulation_use: Use verified NJDOH reports as coarse staffing-availability context for RWJUH and Saint Peter’s, preserving hospital, unit, quarter, and staff-category distinctions. Build the ED journey task-dependency inventory as an explicitly unmeasured workflow structure; mark durations and staffing requirements pending. Do not infer local care minutes from ratios. If quantitative task-time distributions are needed before institutional collection, search separately for a reviewed national/external study or benchmark and label its population and transfer limits.
limitations: This is candidate-source discovery, not dataset acquisition; no records were downloaded or acquired.
The only inspected quantitative public source is staffing coverage at coarse unit/shift or ED daily summary grains.
No verified source in the inspected pages supplied direct local task durations or the complete nursing/allied-health/interpreter task mix.
Source and domain-owner applicability and rights review remain required.
